$$ \angle R = 180^\circ - (\angle P + \angle Q) $$
$$ \angle R = 180^\circ - (40^\circ + 35^\circ) $$

$$ \angle R = 105^\circ $$

**Step 2: Use the parallel line property to find $\angle STR$.**

Consider the line segment $\overline{PR}$ as a transversal that intersects the parallel lines $\overline{ST}$ and $\overline{QR}$.
The angle $\angle STR$ and the angle $\angle PRQ$ (which is $\angle R$) are consecutive interior angles (also called same-side interior angles) because they lie on the same side of the transversal $\overline{PR}$ and between the parallel lines.
Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, meaning their sum is $180^\circ$.

Therefore:
$$ \angle STR + \angle R = 180^\circ $$
$$ \angle STR + 105^\circ = 180^\circ $$

$$ \angle STR = 75^\circ $$

So, $\angle PST = 35^\circ$.
Now, consider $\triangle PST$. The angle $\angle STR$ is an exterior angle to $\triangle PST$ at vertex $T$ (since $P, T, R$ are collinear). By the Exterior Angle Theorem, the measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.
$$ \angle STR = \angle P + \angle PST $$
$$ \angle STR = 40^\circ + 35^\circ $$
$$ \angle STR = 75^\circ $$

Both methods yield the same result.
